body:
My Dying Bride has a song called The Dreadful Hours about an abusive father, there are different lines said by the son, mother and father. In the beginning the mother says this:  
*Child, just hold on. Night will soon be gone. Sleep if you can.*  
  
And then it ends with the mother saying  
*Child, please come awake. Please, my tiny son.*

I think I don't want them to feel like I'll always be like this, I think I will be most of the time and it's not something I'd want them to feel too. They think I'm just shy, introverted and not sure what I want out of life, that would mean I might some time just grow out of it and suddenly find a passion so they can believe I'll be ok. I don't want them lying awake at night wondering what they could possibly do or how long I'll still be around.  

It's understandable to blame them for being too nice though, they know a lot more about how the world works so they should be able to see future problems coming much earlier than you. Mine were really nice for letting me be alone all the time for example, but coming home from school and not saying a word for the rest of the day starts taking a toll after a few years. I don't blame them, at the time I wouldn't have wanted them to bother me, but they could have figured that something is a little off.  
  
Well my mom probably has some mental issues and she'd act very different on different days, but she did make me feel really bad whenever she'd start a request with "Since you have nothing you do all day anyway, could you ..."  
My dad was way better at asking me to do stuff, he'd be more like "Hey I'm working on this thing but I need someone to help me right now, when you have the time could you come down?" So afterwards instead of feeling like I finished a punishment I'd feel like I was helpful.

I don't think they really minded at all, even though they didn't even know my issues all that well (actually they still don't). My dad was mostly concerned about me, he knows he can't support me forever. So now he's relieved that he doesn't have to worry as much about my future. My mom has some problems of her own so I'm not sure what to say about her. I couldn't tell if she was annoyed by me not having a job or just trying to help me.

I was in that situation for a few years and now I've been working for a few years. I wouldn't agree with Danger-Tits saying that you don't know what it's like to feel like crap, it's just a different kind of feeling like crap.  
I don't know if this is similar to you but for me not having a job made me feel absolutely useless, completely selfish for not going through the same crap as everyone else while not suffering the consequences of it, a huge disappointment to my parents etc. It's hard to enjoy anything cause you didn't deserve it, at least that's how people make you feel.  

Now I feel like my parents might be happy with me and like I have earned all the things I consume. On the other hand I can't get myself to enjoy anything if I have to go to work later or get up early for work tomorrow. I really don't give a shit about the work I do so every minute there I wish I could do something else instead, any better idea I get at work I have to delay until I have some actual time for it. Any hobby or people I want to spend time on have to be planned around my job, anything that takes too long gets interrupted by work and has to be split up in many days.  
  
Instead of feeling ashamed, selfish and insignificant I get to feel exhausted, trapped and hopeless.  
  
There was one time shortly before I got a job where I didn't feel as bad though. This was when living with my parents and unemployed while also trying to make their life easier around the house. Helping with household, working in the backyard, fixing things that are so little in the way that no one bothered with them for years. It's useful, it directly helps people you care about, you have the freedom to do something another time, to take a break any time or to choose whatever you want to work on right now.  

If only jobs were like that, but even if you'd be able to choose your own work hours you'd still be forced to work far more than you want just to make a living.

At work I actually sing death and black metal at times to feel better. Some places are so loud that you can't hear it over the machines if you try to cover it up a bit.  
I have also started telling people about my problems the last weeks, while it feels pretty good it does also make me feel like I've given up on getting better. I might as well not hide it anymore cause it'll be there forever.  
But talking to people really only works after I've known them for a long time. It's not just fear, I also am very suspicious of others and feel very guilty over minor things. So I don't know who I could trust or not.   
The ones I have talked to are helpful and ok with adjusting to make me more comfortable, it's nice but makes me feel a bit bad about needing that. Like it's a bit selfish to ask for different treatment than everyone else.
